map.prompt:
Generate one image and save it as clockwork-carnival--world-map.png in the current directory.

A world map for a tabletop role-playing campaign, landscape 3:2, seen straight from above like a hand-painted illustrated map (orthographic top-down view, no perspective, no horizon, no sky). A top-down illustrated map of a festive country road winding between rolling green hills, seen straight from above, dominated by an enormous brass-and-copper walking casino facing right. The casino's body fills the left two thirds: at its left end a rear deck of tethered wicker balloon baskets under striped parasols; in the upper left a steamy laundry of foaming tubs with masks drying on lines; in the lower left a counting room with a brass counter and coloured cases; at the centre a round salon with velvet tables ringed around a dais under a gilded dome; above it, toward the top, an accordion-folded mirrored balcony with a big brass dial; in the lower middle a grand arch of stacked top hats with coat-stands and a folding stair; at the right end an open front deck with three steps up to a turntable dais under a glass bell. Eight jointed copper legs in two rows stand out from its sides, round feet on the road. In the lower left corner, market stalls and a wagon with fluttering coloured ribbons. To the right the road dips into a narrow windless ravine and climbs onto a copper-green plain, ending at a long rampart of green copper plates near the right edge. No people, no text.

Draw every place described above as a small, clearly recognisable landmark exactly at its stated position, with the roads, paths, corridors or waterways between them visible, so that markers can later be pinned on each landmark. Fill the whole picture edge to edge with the mapped land (no border, no frame, no cartouche, no legend, no compass rose, no scale bar, no grid). Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, labels or symbols that read as letters anywhere on the map. No people, no creatures, no figures.

The attached image is this campaign's cover: match its painting technique, palette, light and mood, but not its composition.

Match one consistent house style: original premium illustrated comic-fantasy caper for ages 12 and up, painterly gouache and ink with confident visible brushwork, crisp readable silhouettes and subtle paper grain, lively theatrical staging like a stage play caught mid-scene, warm festive lantern light; palette of polished copper and brass, lacquer goose red, carnival teal and mint, cream masks and ivory ribbons, with deep plum-brown shadows. Recurring details: gears and cogs, festive half-masks. Show a red clockwork goose only when the prompt asks for it. Mischief, wit and warm humanity; no horror, no gore, no franchise references, no anime look, no photorealism. No text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no border.
